subject: ProofChain: subprocessor evidence ingestion and CAIQ mapping
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@novared.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: ProofChain: request to ingest subprocessor evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this on. We are kicking off a SOC 2 re-audit and we need a structured handoff of Redwood's subprocessor evidence so our third-party risk platform can ingest and validate it. Specifically we need: 

- A machine-readable subprocessor roster (name, service, region, data classification, residency, encryption-in-transit, encryption-at-rest, KMS residency)
- Per-subprocessor CAIQ mappings (columns to indicate yes/no/partial for the standard CAIQ controls)
- Representative evidence files (S3 or signed PDFs) or SHA256 hashes of those files for chain-of-custody validation

Is there a preferred artifact format you can provide? Ideally our intake expects a CSV plus a zipped evidence bundle, but we can accept Drive links and hashed manifests.

We'd also like an estimated SLAT for delivery (aiming for 7 business days if possible). Looping in our procurement lead (Nick Bell) on CC so they can coordinate DocuSign LOA if required.

Appreciate it —
Alyssa Chen
Compliance Manager, NovaRed Health
alyssa.chen@novared.com
[Attachment stub: request_form_fillable.pdf (PDF)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@novared.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0000
Subject: Re: ProofChain: request to ingest subprocessor evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear checklist. We're prepared to deliver a ProofChain package that meets the requirements you listed. Summary of our proposed artifacts and timeline: 

- Deliverables: 
  * subprocessor_proofchain_manifest_v1.csv (CSV with the fields you requested)
  * evidence bundle (zipped) + per-file SHA256 manifest
  * CAIQ mapping PDF (per-subprocessor answers)
- Timeline: initial package within 5 business days, follow-up clarifications/notes within 2 business days after that (total 7 business days max)
- Format: CSV + Drive link + SHA256 manifest. We can also provide individual signed PDFs for select subprocessors on request.

I attached an initial manifest (v1) for your intake team to preview — it's intentionally conservative on residency flags; we can expand entries if you need more granularity. Marissa (Security) will add CAIQ mapping and evidence pointers. Grace from Customer Success is included to coordinate anything that requires product entitlements or on-prem packaging.

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link/proofchain-manifest
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/ticket/NR-9876

Next steps: please confirm (1) whether hashed evidence is acceptable for your ingestion, and (2) whether you prefer a DocuSign LOA prior to evidence transfer. Once we have that we'll proceed with the full bundle.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
[Attachment stub: subprocessor_proofchain_manifest_v1.csv (CSV)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@novared.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 08:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: ProofChain: request to ingest subprocessor evidence for SOC 2 / CAIQ mapping

Hi Alyssa / Rafael — looping in some specifics on the security side.

Quick answers up front: hashed evidence is fine for bulk ingestion and chain-of-custody validation; for a small subset of high-risk subprocessors (payment processors, KMS providers) we can provide signed PDFs or CA-signed attestations.

Notes on the manifest and CAIQ mapping approach: 
- We'll populate a CAIQ mapping PDF where each control line references the supporting evidence file name and SHA256.
- Suggested CSV schema (we used these columns in the attached manifest): subprocessor_name, service_description, dataclass, residency, encryption_in_transit (Y/N), encryption_at_rest (Y/N), kms_owner, access_model (shared/dedicated), evidence_reference, caiq_mapping_ref
- For evidence transfer we prefer an encrypted S3 upload (pre-signed URL) or a secured Drive folder with restricted access. If NovaRed's intake system requires a different method, we can adapt.

Clarifying question for NovaRed: do you need explicit IP addresses or hostnames for any subprocessors, or is the service-level residency and encryption stance sufficient?

I'm attaching the CAIQ mapping draft and an access matrix demonstrating role-scoped access to each subprocessor.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security Compliance, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
[Attachment stub: access_matrix_v2.xlsx (XLSX)]
[Attachment stub: sig_mapping_answers.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks, Marissa and Rafael — this all looks good. A few quick confirmations: 

- Hashed evidence is acceptable for our automated ingestion pipeline; for KMS and payment providers we'll request signed PDFs (we can flag those with a separate field in the manifest).
- DocuSign LOA before transfer is preferred by procurement (Nick on CC). Please prepare a simple LOA that allows NovaRed Security to ingest and retain hashed evidence for audit purposes.
- We can take an encrypted pre-signed S3 upload; if Redwood wants to share via Drive, please set folder ACLs to NovaRed staff only and provide the SHA256 manifest.

Can we schedule a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow at 15:00 PT to verify column mappings? Nick will also join to confirm LOA language.

Regards,
Alyssa Chen
Compliance Manager, NovaRed Health
